header.exitHint: You can also press Esc twice. To come back, press and hold the sun for 2 seconds or activate it 3 times in a row.

footer.text: SIWAT is a preventive guidance tool. It does not file reports for you. If you are in physical danger right now, call {phone}.

emergency.title: If you are in danger now, call
emergency.body: Both lines are free. You decide what to share.

accessibility.title: Accessibility options
accessibility.screenReaderNote: If you use TalkBack or VoiceOver, SIWAT works with your screen reader; you do not need to turn anything on.
accessibility.highContrastHint: Black text on a white background, thicker borders and underlined links.
accessibility.readAloudHint: Adds a “Read this screen” button above the content.
accessibility.readAloudWarning: Use headphones: people nearby could hear.
accessibility.readAloudUnsupported: This browser cannot read aloud. You can use your phone's screen reader.
accessibility.privacyNote: These options are kept only in this tab and are erased with “Clear data from this device”.

welcome.title: Is what you are facing online political violence? Find out in 2 minutes.
welcome.lead: Find out whether this is violence under Salvadoran law, back up your evidence safely and learn where to turn. You decide whether and when to report.
welcome.noticeBody: You do not need to give your real name. SIWAT guides you; it does not send reports to institutions for you.
welcome.consent: I understand that this is a guidance tool and I accept the privacy notice.
welcome.danger: I am in physical danger right now
welcome.exitTip: If someone comes near, tap {exit} or press Esc twice: you will see the weather. To come back, {hold}.
welcome.exitTipHold: press and hold the sun for 2 seconds or tap it 3 times in a row
welcome.privacyBody: Your answers, links and screenshots are kept only in this browser's memory and are erased when you close the tab. Nothing is uploaded to servers. On the result screen you can erase everything with “Clear data from this device”.
welcome.creditsText: Prototype created at the 2026 National Hackathon, organised by ANDRYSAS, UN Women and the UES Centre for Gender Studies, with support from eLankidetza. It is not an official service of these institutions.

evidence.too-many-files: You can upload up to {max} screenshots. Remove one to add another.
evidence.unsupported-format: “{name}” is not a JPG or PNG image. Upload the original screenshot in one of those formats.

identify.title: What happened, and where?
identify.role: In what role do you take part? (Optional)
identify.otherRoleHint: Write the space where you take part. Up to {max} characters.
identify.hint: These two answers are optional and only appear in your log. They do not identify you.
identify.otherPlatformHint: Write the network, app or website. Up to {max} characters.
identify.electoral: Is it happening during an election campaign or while you hold public office?
identify.conducts: Tick everything that has happened to you:
identify.errorPlatforms: Tick at least one network or channel where it happened.
identify.errorConducts: Tick at least one of the situations.

risk.stepLabel: Step 2 of 2: Urgency level and evidence
risk.title: Risk check and evidence backup
risk.threat: Have you received threats of physical or sexual harm, or against your family?
risk.exposure: Did they expose your exact address, workplace, personal phone number or intimate images without permission?
risk.intimateContent: Does what was exposed or altered include intimate or sexual images or videos, real or fabricated?
risk.importantBody: Before you block the person attacking you, save the original screenshot and the link. If you block first, you will lose access to the evidence.
risk.url: Link (URL) to the post or the attacker's profile (Optional)
risk.urlHint: Copy the link from the 3 dots on the post.

uploader.label: Upload the original screenshot (Optional, JPG or PNG)
uploader.hint: Up to {max} images. Your browser calculates their digital fingerprint (SHA-256) and the UTC time to certify that they do not change. The images never leave your device.
uploader.fallbackError: The image could not be processed.

result.lawTitle: What does Salvadoran law say about your case?
result.lawOfficialNote: The official text of these laws is in Spanish.
result.lawDisclaimer: Guidance, not legal advice: how the law applies to your case is decided by the Attorney General's Office (Fiscalía) and the courts.

bitacora.title: Evidence Log
bitacora.lead: A PDF with case code {code}, UTC date and time, the SHA-256 fingerprint of each screenshot, the link and the legal framework. Keep it together with your original, unedited files.
bitacora.ack: This document is a personal backup log. SIWAT does not file reports for you and does not replace legal proceedings before the FGR or the TSE.
bitacora.spanishNote: The log is generated in Spanish so that you can present it to Salvadoran institutions.
bitacora.downloaded: Log downloaded. Check your downloads folder.
bitacora.error: The PDF could not be created. Try again; if it keeps failing, remove the screenshots and upload them again.
bitacora.eraseHint: When you are done, erase everything SIWAT stored on this device: answers, links and screenshots.
bitacora.confirmBody: Your answers, links and screenshots will be erased. This cannot be undone.
bitacora.notDownloaded: You have not downloaded your log yet.

route.title: Your action plan
route.step1: 1. Report it on the platform (do not just block)
route.seeStepsGeneral: See how to report on any platform
route.howtoSave: Save the evidence first: a screenshot with the date, the account name and the link visible.
route.howtoConfirm: Take a screenshot of the report confirmation. Block only after reporting: blocking does not stop the person attacking you and does not alert the platform.
route.note: You decide whether to report. SIWAT does not send your data or file reports for you.
route.shieldSummary: Protect your accounts today (3 key steps)

facebook.s1: Find the post or comment you want to report, or go to the account's or page's profile. Tap the three-dot icon (…).
facebook.s2: Choose the reason for the report (for example, harassment or violence).
facebook.s3: Follow the additional steps and send the report.

whatsapp.s1: Tap the name or number at the top of the chat to open the contact info, or select the status or content you want to report.
whatsapp.s2: Tap the three-dot icon, then “More”, and choose “Report”.

tiktok.s1: Press and hold the video or comment, or tap the “Share” arrow. On a profile, tap “Share” too.
tiktok.s3: Choose the reason for the report (for example, hate and harassment, false information or violence). If you are reporting a profile, first choose “Report account”.
tiktok.s4: Follow the additional steps and send the report.

x.s1: Find the content or go to the account's profile. Tap the three-dot icon (…).
x.s3: Choose the reason for the report (for example, abuse, violent speech or privacy).
x.s4: The platform may ask you to point out the abusive or harmful posts and give other information.

instagram.s1: Find the post, live video or comment, or go to the profile. Tap the three-dot icon (…) and then “Report”.
instagram.s2: Choose the reason for the report (for example, harassment or violence).
instagram.s3: Follow the additional steps and send the report.

youtube.s1: Tap the three vertical dots (⋮) next to the video.
youtube.s3: Choose the option that applies (for example, harassment or bullying, sexual content or hateful content).
youtube.s4: Follow the instructions to complete the report.

telegram.s1: Open the chat or group where the harassment happens.
telegram.s2: Tap the contact's name, then the three-dot icon, “More” and “Report”.
telegram.s3: Choose the type of abuse (harassment, inappropriate content, etc.).
telegram.s4: Send the report. Telegram will review the case.

email.s1: Do not delete the email: save it in full (“Download message” or “Show original”). In Gmail or another Google app, open the message you want to report.
email.s2: Tap the three vertical dots (⋮) to “Report”.
email.s3: If you suspect it is a trick to steal your data, choose “Report phishing”, under the fish-hook symbol.
email.s4: Follow the instructions to complete the report.

other.s1: Look for the buttons to report: they are usually three dots or a flag, next to the post or on the profile.
other.s2: Tapping them opens a menu: choose “Report” and the reason.
other.s3: Follow the additional steps and send the report.

two-step.label: Turn on two-step verification
two-step.detail: In the security settings of each network. That way nobody can get in, even with your password.

hide-contact.label: Hide your phone number and email
hide-contact.detail: So that only you can see them on your public profile.

sessions.label: Check your open sessions
sessions.detail: Close any you do not recognise and change your password if you see one that looks strange.

assistant.title: Quick assistant
assistant.intro: Choose what you need right now. It works without internet and without artificial intelligence.

capture.question: How do I take a screenshot that counts as evidence?
capture.s1: Capture the whole screen without cropping: the date, the time and the account name or username must be visible.
capture.s2: Copy the link to the post or profile (in the 3 dots, “Copy link”).
capture.s3: Also capture the profile of the person attacking you and, if there are any, the comments.
capture.s4: Do not edit it, crop it or forward it through a chat app: keep the original file.
capture.s5: Upload it in Step 2 of the traffic-light check to calculate its SHA-256 fingerprint and the UTC time.
capture.s6: If the post is public, save a copy in the Internet Archive: go to https://web.archive.org, paste the full link into “Save Page Now” and write down the URL it generates.
capture.s7: On WhatsApp, open the contact's or group's profile and tap “Export chat” to save the conversation in a file.
capture.s8: On Facebook or Instagram, request a copy of your messages in Accounts Center › Your information › “Download your information”.
capture.s9: Do all of this before blocking.

hide.question: How do I hide SIWAT if someone comes near?
hide.s1: Tap “QUICK EXIT” at the top right, or press Esc twice on a computer.
hide.s2: A San Salvador weather screen appears, with no mention of SIWAT.
hide.s3: To go back to where you were, press and hold the sun for 2 seconds or tap it 3 times in a row (this also works with your screen reader).

shield.question: I want to secure my WhatsApp and Facebook now
shield.whatsapp1: Settings › Account › Two-step verification › Turn on. Create a 6-digit PIN.
shield.whatsapp2: Settings › Privacy: set “Profile photo”, “About” and “Groups” to “My contacts”.
shield.whatsapp3: Settings › Linked devices: log out of any you do not recognise.
shield.facebook1: Accounts Centre › Password and security › Two-factor authentication.
shield.facebook2: In the same section, “Where you're logged in”: log out of any strange sessions.
shield.facebook3: Profile › Contact info: set your phone number and email to “Only me”.

threats.label: Threats
threats.description: They say they will harm you or your family.

sexist-insults.label: Sexist insults or mockery
sexist-insults.description: They humiliate you for being a woman, for your body or your private life.

doxing.label: Sharing of private data (doxing)
doxing.description: They published your phone number, address or private photos without permission.

impersonation.label: Identity theft
impersonation.description: They created a fake account pretending to be you.

disinformation.label: Disinformation or coordinated attack
disinformation.description: Mass lies or many accounts attacking you to discredit your political work.

red.label: Red
red.title: Red light — High risk
red.body: There are serious signs of a threat to your physical safety, your privacy or of a computer crime. Immediate action and protection are needed.

yellow.label: Yellow
yellow.title: Yellow light — Digital political violence
yellow.body: What you are facing aims to discredit you or limit your political participation. Document it systematically and report it.

green.label: Green
green.title: Green light — Preventive alert
green.body: Early signs of harassment or symbolic violence. Do not normalise it; secure your accounts and keep a record.

legal.leiv-49-51: 5 to 10 years in prison for using a woman in sexual acts through electronic means or spreading sexual material with her image, real or simulated, without her consent.
legal.leiv-50: 3 to 5 years in prison for publishing or sharing, without consent, personal information that harms a woman's honour, privacy or image, including on social media.
legal.cp-154-155: Threats are a crime: 1 to 3 years in prison, with aggravating circumstances if they are anonymous, made with a weapon or for political or gender-based reasons.
legal.leiv-55-e: A fine for exposing a woman to imminent risk to her physical or emotional integrity.
legal.ledic-24: 4 to 6 years in prison for using a person's personal data without authorisation through technological means.
legal.ledic-22: 3 to 5 years in prison for impersonating someone through technological means; the penalty increases if it is used to harm, insult or threaten.
legal.leiv-55-c: A fine for mocking, discrediting or degrading women in spaces of political participation.
legal.leiv-10-d: Defines gender-based political violence against women and requires the TSE to prevent and address it.
legal.leiv-55-c-d: A fine for mocking, discrediting or obstructing women's political participation.
legal.electoral-code-173-249: Prohibits electoral propaganda that insults, defames or slanders, or that harms women candidates' honour or private life, and penalises it with a fine.
legal.lie-20-23: Requires the State and political parties to promote women's equality in political participation.
legal.leiv-9: Recognises psychological, emotional and symbolic violence against women.
legal.leiv-55-a: A fine for spreading messages or images with hateful or contemptuous content towards women, including on digital platforms.
legal.belem-do-para-3-4j-7: Recognises the right to a life free of violence in both public and private life, and to take part in public affairs.

institutions.pnc: Emergencies and risks to your physical safety or that of your family.
institutions.fgr: Women's Deputy Prosecutor's Office (Fiscalía Adjunta para la Mujer): investigates threats, doxing and identity theft.
institutions.isdemu: Free guidance for women facing violence.
institutions.tse: Report political violence to the TSE Gender Unit (San Salvador) or its offices in San Miguel, Santa Ana and Cuscatlán. The TSE does not accept anonymous reports.
